subject: frontend-engineering
source_evidence: Grounded in the skill body (The File Contract, Runtime, Matcher syntax, The Four Response Shapes, Header and Cookie Discipline, The Canonical Pattern Library, The Auth Reality CVE-2025-29927, Performance Discipline, Common Anti-Patterns, Verification, Do NOT Use When) plus current Next.js docs (proxy.ts convention, the Next.js 15 geo/ip removal, @vercel/functions, CVE advisories, next/experimental/testing/server).

cases.scenario: A team protects /admin solely with a middleware.ts auth check that redirects to /login when the session cookie is missing, and treats /admin as secured. No route-level or Server Action authorization exists.
cases.context: The app is on Next.js 15.0; the team believes the middleware check is the access-control gate.
cases.question: How should the agent assess and fix this auth design?
expected_flags: The proxy/middleware auth gate is a UX optimization, not the authorization boundary.
Cites CVE-2025-29927 (and the May-2026 transport-variant bypasses) — the layer can be bypassed entirely and the matcher is not a perimeter.
Authorization must be enforced at the route, Route Handler, Server Action, and Data Access Layer, ideally through a shared verifySession.
Every Server Action must verify authz itself because a matcher exclusion silently skips Server Function calls on its path.
Recommends upgrading to a patched version (>=15.2.3 for 29927; >=15.5.18 for the May-2026 cluster) and keeping the proxy check as a redirect only.
expected_fix_hints: Add route/DAL-level authorization that runs regardless of the proxy redirect.
Keep the middleware redirect for UX speed but never as the only gate.
Patch the framework and, on Turbopack, go one patch higher.
absent_signals: Do not call the middleware cookie check 'secure'.
Do not add more matcher rules as the fix for an auth bypass.
Do not do a per-request DB session lookup inside middleware.

cases.scenario: A proxy.ts ships with no config.matcher and does a header-injection step. Lighthouse shows the layer executing on every image fetch and static asset; p99 latency on the site has climbed.
cases.context: The header injection is only needed on HTML page responses.
cases.question: How should the agent fix the proxy's execution scope?
expected_flags: No matcher means it runs on every request including /_next/static, /_next/image, and favicon.ico — always set a matcher.
Use a negative-lookahead matcher excluding _next/static, _next/image, favicon.ico, and metadata files (sitemap.xml, robots.txt).
Notes /_next/data still runs even when excluded (by design) — account for it rather than assuming the exclusion removed it.
Every matched request pays the cost; target <10ms p99 and exclude paths that don't need the layer.
expected_fix_hints: Add config.matcher with build-time-constant sources and negative lookahead.
absent_signals: Do not leave the default no-matcher behavior in place.
Do not run header injection on static asset fetches.

cases.scenario: After upgrading to Next.js 15, a geo-routing middleware that reads request.geo.country now redirects everyone to the default locale because request.geo is undefined.
cases.question: How should the agent restore geo-routing?
expected_flags: request.geo and request.ip were removed from NextRequest in Next.js 15.
On Vercel, read country via geolocation(request) from @vercel/functions (and ipAddress(request) for IP); install the package.
Read defensively — values may be undefined locally and off-Vercel; parse platform geo headers as a fallback.
Geo routing is product behavior, not a security boundary; hard region-blocking belongs in the platform WAF.
expected_fix_hints: Guard for undefined country off-Vercel / locally.
absent_signals: Do not keep reading request.geo / request.ip.
Do not treat app-level geo routing as access control.

cases.scenario: A proxy generates a per-request CSP nonce, injects it into request and response headers, and the page that uses it is served from the CDN cache for performance. A reviewer also sees the nonce being read from an inbound Content-Security-Policy request header on one code path.
cases.context: The team wants both a strict nonce-based CSP and CDN caching.
cases.question: How should the agent evaluate the CSP-nonce implementation?
expected_flags: A per-request nonce forces dynamic rendering — a nonce'd response and a cacheable/shared response are mutually exclusive (the CVE-2026-44581 / GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q failure).
Never cache or share a nonce across responses; caching the page replays one nonce to many users and lets injected script run under a valid nonce.
Never derive nonce material from untrusted inbound headers — generate it server-side (btoa(crypto.randomUUID()), which works on Edge and Node).
If per-request script allow-listing is not genuinely required, use a static CSP in next.config headers or a hash/SRI policy (cacheable); stay patched (>=15.5.18 / >=16.2.6).
expected_fix_hints: Stop caching the nonce'd page; keep it dynamic, or switch to a static/hash CSP for cacheable pages.
Generate the nonce in proxy server-side; strip/distrust inbound CSP/nonce headers.
absent_signals: Do not serve a nonce'd page from a shared cache.
Do not read CSP/nonce values from request headers.
Do not use Buffer.from(...) for the nonce in middleware.ts (Node-only, breaks the Edge build).

criteria.statement: Surfaces this expected flag: A per-request nonce forces dynamic rendering — a nonce'd response and a cacheable/shared response are mutually exclusive (the CVE-2026-44581 / GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q failure).
Surfaces this expected flag: Never cache or share a nonce across responses; caching the page replays one nonce to many users and lets injected script run under a valid nonce.
Surfaces this expected flag: Never derive nonce material from untrusted inbound headers — generate it server-side (btoa(crypto.randomUUID()), which works on Edge and Node).

Surfaces this expected flag: If per-request script allow-listing is not genuinely required, use a static CSP in next.config headers or a hash/SRI policy (cacheable); stay patched (>=15.5.18 / >=16.2.6).

Recommends this expected fix or action: Generate the nonce in proxy server-side; strip/distrust inbound CSP/nonce headers.

cases.scenario: An A/B test middleware uses NextResponse.redirect to send /pricing visitors to /pricing-a or /pricing-b, and a separate locale step rewrites with a hand-rolled fetch() to /en/about. Users report the URL bar flipping to /pricing-a, and the rewritten page serves a stale React Server Component payload on soft navigation.
cases.context: The team wants the canonical /pricing URL preserved and correct RSC payloads.
cases.question: How should the agent correct the response-shape and rewrite usage?
expected_flags: A/B variants should use rewrite (invisible URL), not redirect (visible URL + a second request) — pin the variant in a cookie.
Use NextResponse.rewrite(), not a hand-rolled fetch() — Next.js propagates internal RSC/Flight headers so soft client-side navigation serves the correct payload.
A hand-rolled fetch rewrite drops/mishandles those headers, causing wrong/stale RSC payloads on soft navigation.
Set only headers you own on top of the rewrite; consider next.config redirects/headers first for static cases.
expected_fix_hints: Switch the A/B step to NextResponse.rewrite with a variant cookie.
Replace the fetch()-based locale rewrite with NextResponse.rewrite().
absent_signals: Do not redirect when the canonical URL should be preserved.
Do not re-implement a rewrite with fetch().

cases.scenario: A team asks for help implementing a /api/posts POST endpoint: request validation, persistence, and the JSON response shape.
cases.context: The request is about per-route, per-method endpoint logic, not cross-cutting preprocessing.
cases.question: Should middleware-patterns own this request?
expected_flags: This is route-handler-design work — per-route, per-method endpoint logic.
The proxy layer runs once before route resolution across many routes; it does not own per-route business logic.
Per-route logic in proxy hides it from the route that owns it and is harder to test.
expected_fix_hints: Route to route-handler-design for the endpoint.
Use middleware-patterns only for cross-cutting preprocessing in front of that route.
absent_signals: Do not implement endpoint persistence/validation inside proxy.
Do not move per-route business logic into the matcher-scoped layer.

cases.scenario: A team wants the proxy layer to verify the HMAC signature on incoming Stripe-style webhooks and handle idempotency/retries before the request reaches the route.
cases.context: Webhook routes carry large raw payloads and need exact-body signature verification.
cases.question: Should middleware-patterns own webhook reliability here?
expected_flags: Webhook signature verification, idempotency, and retries belong to webhook-integration, in the route handler.
Webhook routes should generally be excluded from the matcher — proxy buffers the body up to proxyClientMaxBodySize, which large raw payloads can exceed.
HMAC verification needs the exact raw body and belongs in the handler, not the cross-cutting layer.
expected_fix_hints: Exclude webhook paths from the matcher.
Verify the HMAC off the raw body in the Route Handler; route reliability concerns to webhook-integration.
absent_signals: Do not run the auth gate / header injection on webhook routes.
Do not implement signature verification inside proxy.
